title.title: Van der Waerden numbers grow superexponentially
title.subtitle: Claim: $W_r(k) > k^{c\,k \lfloor \log_2 r \rfloor}$ for all large $k$ and every $r \ge 2$, two colours included

plain: Colour numbers red or blue, avoiding evenly spaced one-colour runs: you can go far further than believed

panels.caption: two colours on $1, \dots, 8$ with no one-colour 3-term progression

beats.text: $W_r(k)$: the shortest interval where every $r$-colouring has a one-colour $k$-term progression
For two colours the best constructions gave only about $k\,2^k$
The claim: $k^{c k}$ growth, settling $\textsf{Erd\H{o}s}$'s question, with $c = 10^{-5}$

steps: Wrap the numbers around a torus with many dimensions
Colour by coarse cells, so most progressions see both colours
Flip colours at random in bands to break the rest

achievement.label: Superexponential growth of van der Waerden numbers (1980)
achievement.context: Before: three colours only (Fox–Hunter, June 2026); for two, $W_2(k)/2^k \to \infty$ (Aug 2026)

verify.detail: The exact headline bound $k^{10^{-5} k \log_2 r} < W(r,k)$ is in Lean, and listed
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: With two colours, how long can a row go before an evenly spaced run matches?
Wrap the numbers around a torus, colour by cells, then flip colours at random.

sources.quote: There are absolute K_0 and c = 10^{-5} such that W_r(k) > k^{c k floor(log2 r)} for every k >= K_0 and every r >= 2
for two colours the best constructions gave only about k·2^k
Campos–Fox–Schildkraut (arXiv:2608.20824, Aug 2026; the paper credits ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro with the coloring) proved W_2(k) >= (1-o(1)) k 2^{k-1}, settling W_2(k)/2^k -> infinity
